title: TERMINOLOGY • The asset that forms the substratum of the forward contract is called the underlying asset. • The underlying assets include stocks, currencies, interest rates, commodities, debt instruments, electricity, insurance payouts, weather etc. • The date on which the forward contract mandates delivery of the underlying asset is called its maturity or exercise date.

PAYOFF & PROFIT DIAGRAM • The price of the underlying invariably evolves as a stochastic process. Hence, its value on the maturity of the derivative is a random variable. The payoff from the derivative is, consequently, the function of a random variable. It is, therefore, useful to ascertain the payoff from the derivative corresponding to different possible values of the underlying's price. This is usually done through payoff diagrams.

FORWARD PRICING: ASSET CLASSIFICATION • Investment assets are assets held by significant numbers of people purely for investment purposes (Examples: gold, silver) • Consumption assets are assets held primarily for consumption (Examples: copper, oil)

PRICING OF FORWARDS PRINCIPLE OF NO ARBITRAGE • Financial assets are packages of risk-return trade-offs. They can be represented by points in two dimensional risk-return space. • Consider two different assets A & B that have absolutely identical maturities, payoffs on maturities (with no intermediate cashflows) and risk-return characteristics. • Then they will command the same price at every instant of time. . If it is not so, an arbitrageur can make an unlimited riskless profit by trading one against the other.
